route.scenario: In 2019, Kavya's NGO paid a vendor to build a volunteer sign-up portal. Today she needs another one.
route.question: How long did it take, and what did it cost, then and now?
route.placeholder: PLACEHOLDER: confirm with a real Tech4Good example
route.reveal: Building got cheap and fast. Thinking about the right problem didn't, and it still matters most.
moderatorTalkingPoints: Where would you spend the time you saved?
Cheap to build means cheap to throw away and try again.

route.scenario: Years ago, Ravi asked a developer for a reminder app for farmers. It took 5 months. The farmers needed voice calls, not an app.
route.question: Where did it go wrong?

steps.text: Ravi writes a brief: build a reminder app

route.reveal: The solution was decided before anyone understood the users. Today Ravi could build a rough version himself in a day, test it with ten farmers, and learn they wanted voice calls.
moderatorTalkingPoints: Who in your organisation understands the problem best, and could they build the first version?

route.board: The person with the problem builds the first version.

route.scenario: In one afternoon, Farida built three rough versions of a donor update page with AI.
route.question: What should she do next?

options.text: Show all three to five donors and watch what they do
Ask the AI which is best

route.reveal: Show, don't spec. Cheap prototypes let real users choose.
moderatorTalkingPoints: When did you last test something before building it fully?

route.board: Someone built the full solution before testing with users. Nobody used it.

poll.question: Best way round it next time?

options.text: Test a rough version with 5 real users first

route.scenario: Every Monday, Sunitha's AI agent reads health workers' WhatsApp reports, compiles them, flags villages with fever spikes, and drafts an alert to the district.
route.question: Where must the agent stop and ask a human?
route.reveal: Agents can act, not just answer. You decide where they must stop and ask a human.
moderatorTalkingPoints: What's one repetitive multi-step task an agent could run for you, and where would you put the checkpoint?

route.shift: AI as a thinking partner, before building.
route.scenario: Prakash typed 'Build me an accessible website.' The AI asked who his users were, and suggested a voice line might serve them better.
route.question: Which first prompt is best?

options.text: Build me an accessible website in Marathi with large text.
Make our website pass accessibility checks.
Here's our problem, who our users are and what they can access. What are my options before we build anything?

route.reveal: Let AI challenge your solution before you build. Sometimes the problem needs something else entirely, and the users should test whatever you build.
moderatorTalkingPoints: Accessibility means disability, language and literacy. Who tests your tools?

route.shift: Anyone can ship, so check before you share.
route.scenario: Vikram vibe-coded a camera-trap dashboard over the weekend and wants to share it.
route.question: Pick the 4 most important checks before he shares it.

items.text: No secret keys inside the code
Get a second pair of eyes

route.reveal: Vibe coding works. Safety checks are now your job.
moderatorTalkingPoints: What would be the worst thing if your app's link got forwarded?

tips: Paste it into AI and ask it to explain in simple words.

route.shift: From tool users to tool makers.
route.scenario: Aman is teaching 20 colleagues to build their own small tools with AI.
route.question: Rank these first builds from lowest to highest risk.

items.text: Public FAQ page about government schemes
Loan system with members' personal details

route.reveal: Everyone can build. Start where the data is public, then level up with help.
moderatorTalkingPoints: What's a safe first build for your team?

rounds.text: A list of beneficiaries with phone numbers

route.scenario: The village wants its oral histories transcribed with AI, but some stories are sacred.
route.question: Where should each one go?

buckets.text: Offline AI on our own laptop

items.text: Festival songs meant for the public
Elders' everyday life stories, shared with consent
Names and ages of the storytellers

route.reveal: Open-source AI can run offline on a laptop, so sensitive knowledge stays in the community's hands. And the community decides what is shared at all.

route.prompt: Turn to your neighbour: what problem would you solve yourself?

route.scenario: Six months after a volunteer built Shabana's WhatsApp catalogue, the volunteer leaves and it breaks.
route.question: What should the collective do?

options.text: Fix it ourselves with AI, written notes on how it works, and community help

route.reveal: Building is easy now. Keeping it running is the new skill: keep it simple, write it down, find your community.
moderatorTalkingPoints: Share a real Tech4Good story here.

route.board: Keep it simple, document it, find your community.
